results.summary_before: This accelerator calculates the Mandelbrot set iteration z = z^2 + c using 32-bit IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic, performing one iteration per clock cycle. It accepts the complex number c via a shift register interface and outputs the iteration count and an unbounded flag when the result exceeds the bound. The design requires no external hardware and was tested by generating a 256x256 image of the Mandelbrot set, taking about 24 minutes when manually clocked. It is notable for implementing floating-point arithmetic in a compact hardware design.

results.summary_before: This design implements a UART menu system that waits for user input characters (1-7) and responds with either informative text or toggles output bits. It uses a basic UART driver for TX and RX, operating at 115200 bps with a 50 MHz clock, and requires an external UART transceiver connected to the recommended pins. Two output pins can drive LEDs through MOSFET drivers, and the design is controlled by sending single characters without line endings. The documentation is minimal but provides enough information to understand and test the functionality.

The documentation is minimal and the design is very simple, with no external hardware required beyond the clock and input switches.

The design is notable as a beginner-friendly educational project and has been verified by several testers. No complex external hardware is required beyond the LEDs.

results.summary_before: This project implements grayscale conversion and Sobel filtering for edge detection in images. Pixels are sent via SPI, and the processing mode is selected through input pins, with options for bypass, grayscale, Sobel, or combined grayscale and Sobel. An internal LFSR can generate test pixels. The design requires an external SPI master, such as a Raspberry Pi, to send and receive data.
